topic: The Rule of 72: divide 72 by a yearly growth rate to estimate how many years money takes to double (example: 72 / 8 = 9 years).

episode.title: The Rule of 72: A Doubling Shortcut

shots.narration: How long could money take to double? Coin knows a shortcut.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, bright 3D animated city flat, clean desk with two identical clear jars holding different amounts of blank silver tokens; no text or symbols.
shots.action: Kash points between the two jars.
shots.mood: Curious wide eyes, warm daylight, cheerful colours.

shots.narration: Kash wants her example savings to double, without guessing.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, modern flat desk, one jar containing four blank silver tokens, one empty matching jar, open notebook with blank pages.
shots.action: Kash scratches her head above the notebook.
shots.mood: Gentle puzzlement, raised eyebrows, soft pastel surroundings.

shots.narration: [excited] Coin teaches Kash the Rule of seventy-two.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, bright 3D flat, clear token jar and blank notebook on a tidy desk; no writing anywhere.
shots.action: Coin raises one tiny finger beside Kash.
shots.mood: Friendly confidence, cheerful smile, bright golden highlights.

shots.narration: Divide seventy-two by a yearly growth rate to estimate doubling time.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, overhead-style view of the clean desk, blank silver tokens arranged in small equal clusters beside the jar; no numbers or labels.
shots.action: Coin sweeps one arm across the token clusters.
shots.mood: Clear and orderly, inviting colours, attentive expressions.

shots.narration: For example, use eight percent yearly growth.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, modern flat desk, eight plain blue beads arranged in a ring beside the clear savings jar; all surfaces unmarked.
shots.action: Coin points toward the eight blue beads.
shots.mood: Focused curiosity, soft blue accents, friendly smiles.

shots.narration: [surprised] Seventy-two divided by eight estimates nine years to double.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, bright desk with nine evenly spaced blank wooden beads forming a path toward two matching token jars; no text.
shots.action: Coin traces the bead path with one tiny hand.
shots.mood: Delighted discovery, warm gold light, Kash's eyebrows lifted.

shots.narration: That's an estimate, not a promise of growth.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, tidy modern flat, example jars and blank notebook on the desk, uncluttered background.
shots.action: Coin holds up an open palm toward Kash.
shots.mood: Calm and reassuring, gentle smile, balanced soft lighting.

shots.narration: Coin helps Kash picture her example money doubling.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, close view of two identical clear jars, one containing four blank silver tokens and the other eight; no labels.
shots.action: Kash places the eight-token jar beside the four-token jar.
shots.mood: Satisfied understanding, relaxed shoulders, bright friendly colours.

shots.narration: [excited] Try this example today; next, we'll flip the doubling question.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, sunny modern flat desk, blank notebook beside the two example jars, clean unmarked surroundings.
shots.action: Kash slides her blank notebook toward the viewer.
shots.mood: Welcoming invitation, eager smiles, warm hopeful lighting.

episode.endHook: Next episode, we'll flip the doubling question!
episode.description: Coin helps Kash explore the Rule of 72: divide 72 by a yearly growth rate to estimate doubling time. Using eight percent as an example gives nine years—an estimate, not a promise. General money education only.
